description: Computes the true assessable value of excisable goods sold at a cum-duty price by deducting only the effective, actually payable excise duty (post-exemptions), ensuring that theoretical tariff rates or excess collected amounts are not excluded from the taxable base.
application_scenario: Use when an assessee sells goods at a price inclusive of taxes and claims a deduction for excise duty to arrive at the assessable value, particularly when a statutory exemption notification reduces the actual duty liability.
reasoning_flow: Identify the gross wholesale cash price (cum-duty price) charged to the buyer, which inherently includes the element of excise duty alongside other potential deductions.
Deduct all permissible, quantifiable non-duty deductions (e.g., valid trade discounts or transportation costs) from the cum-duty price before calculating the duty component.
Ascertain the effective, actual rate of duty payable after factoring in all applicable statutory exemption notifications, rather than relying on the nominal tariff schedule rate.
Apply the reverse-calculation mathematical formula to the remaining amount to extract the assessable value and the exact duty component based strictly on the effective rate.
Conclude that only the effective duty actually payable can be excluded, and any excess duty collected from the buyer under the guise of taxes forms an inseparable part of the assessable value.
example_application: A manufacturer sells goods at a cum-duty price of Rs. 100. While the schedule tariff rate is 20%, an exemption notification reduces the effective rate to 10%. The manufacturer claims a deduction of 20% to compute the assessable value. The adjudicating authority limits the deduction to the effective 10% actually payable, treating the excess 10% collected as part of the assessable value.
shared_pattern: All three cases address the calculation of assessable value from a cum-duty price by strictly limiting the deduction for excise duty to the effective amount actually payable to the Revenue, establishing the correct mathematical sequence of deductions, and treating any excess collection as part of the taxable value.
scope_exclusions: Do not use for evaluating the substantive eligibility of the exemption itself, or for testing the validity of standard deductions like trade discounts or post-removal expenses.
